slots.title: Fed minutes: unanimous September rate hike
slots.body:
The September Fed meeting minutes describe a unanimous vote to raise interest rates among all nineteen committee participants.

Bloomberg reported that non-voting members joined voting members in backing the hike — a detail markets often watch for splits on how tight policy should stay.

The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 5.3% on the latest daily snapshot in the data (Oct. 6).

Prior session, the S&P 500 closed down 0.2% at 7,801.77.

What part of the minutes are you reading first — labor, inflation, or the path for rates?

slots.title: Trump cool on Iran deal; Brent +2.1%
slots.body:
Brent crude closed up 2.1% at $102.35 in the cross-asset snapshot.

CNBC reported Trump said he is not keen on a deal with Iran, with NBC News citing discussion of possibly resuming large-scale U.S. military operations in the coming weeks.

The same report tied public concern over gasoline and diesel costs to his approval ratings in the data’s summary.

Gold futures were up 0.5% at $4,159.60 in the same window.

Overseas indexes were lower ahead of the U.S. open:
- Nikkei 225 -1.0% to 69,325.85
- Hang Seng -0.9% to 23,910.00
- FTSE 100 -0.8% to 10,458.50

Which headline are you tracking alongside oil — policy, shipping lanes, or fuel prices at the pump?

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 8, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished -0.2% at 7,801.77, off 17.16 points from a prior close of 7,818.93.
The session range was 7,763.34 to 7,807.02.

The Nasdaq Composite matched the S&P’s -0.2% tone, closing at 27,538.69 after a 61.20-point decline.
The intraday band ran 27,341.31 to 27,547.20.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was the weakest major U.S. benchmark in the feed at -0.7%, closing 51,179.87, down 341.41 points.
The Russell 2000 fell -1.3% to 2,793.20, a 37.10-point drop from 2,830.30.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose +0.5% to 15.08, with an intraday high of 16.01 and low of 14.97.

Three high-impact U.S. labor releases were on the calendar for 2026-10-08 at 12:30 p.m.
ET: Initial Jobless Claims (Oct/03), Continuing Jobless Claims (Sep/26), and the four-week average — each listed with prior figures and estimates in the feed, without session actuals in this payload.

Sector averages for Nasdaq-grouped industries on 2026-10-08 put Utilities up +2.3% and Technology up +1.1%.
Healthcare averaged +0.9% and Consumer Cyclical +1.1%.
Real Estate (-1.1%), Basic Materials (-1.0%), Energy (-0.9%), and Industrials (-0.7%) were among the weaker groups.

Meta Platforms closed -2.4% at $721.31, the standout megcap decline in the set.
Eli Lilly rose +2.7% to $1,188.72.
Alphabet Class A shares gained +0.8% to $350.50; Netflix +1.5% to $69.70; Walmart +0.9% to $108.16.

PepsiCo was on the earnings calendar for 2026-10-08 with a listed EPS estimate of $2.29 and revenue estimate near $24.95B; the stock closed -1.6% at $123.73, with a session low of $123.47 matching the year low field in the quote.

Energy equities diverged from Brent: Brent crude was +2.1% at $102.35 while the U.S. Oil Fund ETF was -0.7% at $143.91.
Chevron -1.2% to $205.19 and Exxon Mobil -0.3% to $164.06 rounded out the large-cap energy read in the feed.

Gold futures rose +0.4% to $4,158.90.
The dollar-bullish fund proxy $UUP was +0.5% at $29.04.
Bitcoin USD quoted -0.5% at $82,859.72.

Overseas indexes in the same snapshot showed the Nikkei 225 -1.0% at 69,301.84, FTSE 100 -0.8% at 10,458.50, and Hang Seng -0.9% at 23,911.00.

The latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (dated 2026-10-06) showed the 10-year yield at 5.3% and the 2s10s spread at 0.48 percentage points.
